title: Forms
summary: Reading form fields, the submit event, validation and showing errors.

steps.title: Handling a form
body: // data is { email: "...", age: "..." }: every value is a STRING
- Field values are always **strings** (an empty number field is `""`), so convert and validate.
- HTML attributes like `required` and `type="email"` give quick browser checks, but the **server must validate again**: anyone can send any request.

> **Try it:** open the **Playground**, choose the **HTML/CSS/JS** tab and paste the HTML and script from this card. The live preview runs it in a real browser frame, and the **Tailwind** switch lets you style it with utility classes.

steps.prompt: A number input is left empty. What does `Object.fromEntries(new FormData(form)).age` hold?
steps.explain: Form values are strings. `Number("")` is `0`, which is why you check for the empty string before converting.

steps.title: Validation as a pure function
body: Keep validation separate from the DOM: a function from form data to errors. It is easy to test, and the **same function** can run in the browser and on the server (in Next.js, literally the same file).
if (data.age !== "" && !(Number(data.age) >= 13)) errors.age = "You must be 13 or older";
Returning errors **per field** lets the page show each message next to its input.

steps.explain: An empty age is allowed. `Number("abc")` is `NaN`, and `NaN >= 13` is false, so it fails. A missing email makes `data.email?.includes` give `undefined`, which is falsy.

steps.prompt: Match each form fact to its consequence.
pairs: submit reloads the page by default
errors belong next to their fields
return errors keyed by field name

steps.title: Validate a signup form
prompt: Write `validateSignup(data: Record<string, string>)` returning an object of error messages (empty when valid):
- `email`: must contain one `@` with text on both sides and a `.` after the `@`: `"Enter a valid email"`
- `password`: at least 8 characters **and** at least one digit: `"Password needs 8+ characters and a number"`
- `confirm`: must equal password: `"Passwords do not match"`
Only include keys that have errors.
solution: if (parts.length !== 2 || !parts[0] || !parts[1].includes(".") || parts[1].startsWith(".") || parts[1].endsWith(".")) errors.email = "Enter a valid email";
if (password.length < 8 || !/[0-9]/.test(password)) errors.password = "Password needs 8+ characters and a number";
if ((data.confirm ?? "") !== password) errors.confirm = "Passwords do not match";
template: Dojo.eq("valid", {}, validateSignup({ name: "Ada", email: "ada@math.org", password: "engine42", confirm: "engine42" }));

Dojo.eq("everything wrong", { name: "Name is required", email: "Enter a valid email", password: "Password needs 8+ characters and a number", confirm: "Passwords do not match" }, validateSignup({ name: "  ", email: "ada", password: "short", confirm: "x" }));
Dojo.eq("password without a digit", { password: "Password needs 8+ characters and a number" }, validateSignup({ name: "A", email: "a@b.co", password: "longenough", confirm: "longenough" }));
Dojo.eq("two @", { email: "Enter a valid email" }, validateSignup({ name: "A", email: "a@b@c.com", password: "abcdefg1", confirm: "abcdefg1" }));
Dojo.eq("no dot after @", { email: "Enter a valid email" }, validateSignup({ name: "A", email: "a@localhost", password: "abcdefg1", confirm: "abcdefg1" }));
Dojo.eq("missing fields", { name: "Name is required", email: "Enter a valid email", password: "Password needs 8+ characters and a number" }, validateSignup({}));
hints: `email.split("@")` must give exactly 2 non-empty parts, and the second must contain a `.`.

steps.title: Parse form values
prompt: Form values arrive as strings. Write `parseOrder(data: Record<string, string>)` that returns either `{ ok: true, order }` with typed values or `{ ok: false, errors }` listing the bad field names in order:
- `gift`: a checkbox: present as `"on"` means `true`, missing means `false`
- `note`: optional; trimmed; an empty note becomes `undefined` (leave the key out)
// { ok: true, order: { product: "Tea", qty: 2, gift: true } }
starter: type Order = { product: string; qty: number; gift: boolean; note?: string };
type Parsed = { ok: true; order: Order } | { ok: false; errors: string[] };
solution: type Order = { product: string; qty: number; gift: boolean; note?: string };
type Parsed = { ok: true; order: Order } | { ok: false; errors: string[] };
const order: Order = { product, qty, gift: data.gift === "on" };
template: Dojo.eq("valid with gift", { ok: true, order: { product: "Tea", qty: 2, gift: true } }, parseOrder({ product: " Tea ", qty: "2", gift: "on" }));
Dojo.eq("with a note", { ok: true, order: { product: "Cake", qty: 1, gift: false, note: "no nuts" } }, parseOrder({ product: "Cake", qty: "1", note: "  no nuts " }));
Dojo.eq("blank note dropped", { ok: true, order: { product: "Cake", qty: 1, gift: false } }, parseOrder({ product: "Cake", qty: "1", note: "   " }));
Dojo.eq("bad fields", { ok: false, errors: ["product", "qty"] }, parseOrder({ product: "", qty: "100" }));
Dojo.eq("empty qty", { ok: false, errors: ["qty"] }, parseOrder({ product: "Tea", qty: "" }));
Dojo.eq("fractional qty", { ok: false, errors: ["qty"] }, parseOrder({ product: "Tea", qty: "1.5" }));
hints: Build `order` first, then add `note` only when it is non-empty.
